speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. Can you describe the specific movements you have been experiencing, such as tremors, stiffness, or involuntary jerking, and when did they first start?

speaker: Patient
text: 23-year-old college student. The patient is here for a follow-up appointment. He was recently diagnosed with schizophrenia and started on risperidone approximately 2 months ago. Reports a significant improvement in psychiatric symptoms since the start of treatment.

speaker: Doctor
text: Do you experience a sensation of restlessness or an irresistible urge to move your legs, and have you noticed any rhythmic, repetitive movements like tongue protrusion or lip smacking? REQUEST TEST: Extrapyramidal Symptom Rating Scale

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the normal EPS rating scale despite your new movement symptoms, are you experiencing a subjective sense of inner restlessness or an inability to sit still that worsens when you are at rest? I want to rule out akathisia, which can sometimes present without obvious external tremors or rigidity.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Inability to remain still, persistent feeling of restlessness. I also have Frequent fidgeting, Repetitive crossing and uncrossing of legs, Pacing.

speaker: Doctor
text: Based on your symptoms of inner restlessness and inability to sit still, I am diagnosing you with akathisia, a common side effect of risperidone. DIAGNOSIS READY: Akathisia
